# Fix issue \#520 submission state

> Implement issue #520: “Batch submission state does not update without manual refresh.”
>
> Use our Git methodology. Do not push, merge, modify main, create a PR, or change unrelated work unless I explicitly ask.
>
> Problem:
> After a successful batch submission:
>
> - the Submit button stays visible/enabled;
> - the page does not transition to a completed/submitted state;
> - navigating to the review/list view does not show the new batch until a manual browser refresh.
>
> The likely cause is stale frontend/query/navigation-loader state after a successful submission mutation. Prefer correct local-state updates and query invalidation/refetching; do not use `window.location.reload()` or another forced full-page reload as the fix.
>
> Git workflow:
>
> 1. Read AGENTS.md, frontend contribution guidance, and current test conventions.
> 2. Inspect the working tree and preserve all unrelated local changes. Never reset, clean, stash, or overwrite them.
> 3. Fetch remotes safely and inspect the current main branch plus relevant submission/review frontend code.
> 4. Create and switch to:
>    `graz/fix-submission-state-refresh`
> 5. Trace the complete flow:
>    - submission form/component and Submit-button state;
>    - successful submission mutation/API response;
>    - local submission/batch state;
>    - query cache invalidation/refetch behaviour;
>    - review queue/list query and filters/pagination;
>    - navigation loader/cache behaviour, if applicable.
> 6. Reuse the project’s existing query/state-management conventions. Keep the fix frontend-scoped unless the API response genuinely lacks the data needed for a correct state transition.
> 7. Do not introduce new dependencies.
>
> Required behaviour:
>
> - After confirmed API success, immediately replace/remove/disable the Submit action with a clear submitted/completed state.
> - A batch cannot be submitted again from that same successful UI state.
> - Refresh or invalidate every affected submission/batch query and the review/list query so navigation immediately displays the new batch.
> - Preserve existing filters, pagination, reviewer permissions, and error handling.
> - Failed submissions must retain a retryable, non-success UI state and must not invalidate/pretend success.
> - The user can proceed directly from submission into the review workflow without manually refreshing the browser.
>
> Testing:
>
> 1. Add/update frontend tests proving a successful submission:
>    - changes/removes the Submit action;
>    - displays a clear success/submitted state;
>    - invalidates or updates relevant query state;
>    - displays the new batch on review/list navigation without a browser refresh.
> 2. Add a failure-path test proving the UI does not transition to submitted on an API error.
> 3. Add or update E2E coverage for:
>    `submit batch -> success confirmation -> navigate to review/list -> new batch visible`
> 4. Verify existing filters, pagination, and permission-based review visibility still behave correctly.
> 5. Run relevant frontend unit/integration tests, linting, type checking, and build checks.
>
> Before finishing:
>
> - Inspect `git diff` for unrelated changes and accidental forced-reload logic.
> - Make small, descriptive commits, for example:
>   - `fix(submissions): refresh batch state after submission`
>   - `test(submissions): cover post-submit review visibility`
> - Do not push or open a PR.
>
> Report:
>
> - root cause;
> - exact cache/state queries updated or invalidated;
> - changed files;
> - test commands and results;
> - commit hashes;
> - suggested PR title and description.

Implemented issue #520 on `graz/fix-submission-state-refresh`. No push, merge, PR, or main changes.

Root cause: successful batch uploads set a success result but left the active form/Submit control usable. Batch lists use component-local request state, with no shared cache invalidation.

Fix:
- Successful batch submission now removes the submit action, disables form inputs, and guards against repeat submission.
- Success state provides direct links to the report and submission history.
- Added a lightweight shared batch-collection invalidation signal:
  - submitter history: `listBatches(client)`
  - reviewer pending queue: `listAdminBatches(..., 'awaiting_review')`
  - reviewer history: `listAdminBatches(..., selectedStatus)`
- Reviewer history retains its active status filter when invalidated. Pagination behavior and role gates remain unchanged.
- Failed submissions retain their retryable state and do not invalidate collections.
- No forced reload logic was introduced.

Commits:
- `e3e3fab` `fix(submissions): refresh batch state after submission`
- `c1c45ac` `test(submissions): cover post-submit review visibility`

Changed files include submission/upload pages, batch history/review views, the new collection-state module, unit tests, E2E coverage, and the AI usage register.

Verification passed:
- `npm.cmd run test:frontend` — 165 tests passed
- `npm.cmd run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend`
- `npm.cmd run lint --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend`
- `npm.cmd run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend`
- `PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=4175 npm.cmd run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/submissions.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` — 6 passed

The final diff is clean, scoped to #520, and contains no `window.location.reload()` logic.

Suggested PR title: `#520 Refresh batch state after successful submission`

Suggested PR description: successful uploads now enter a terminal submitted state, invalidate submitter/reviewer batch collections, preserve reviewer filters, and provide immediate history navigation; adds unit and Playwright coverage for post-submit visibility and failure retry behavior.

> where can i check for this fix manually in testing

Run the app, sign in as a submitter/admin, then check:

1. Go to `/submissions/new`.
2. Upload a valid JSON/CSV fixture package (or use Advanced technical JSON as a submitter).
3. After the API returns success, verify:
   - “Fixture upload received” / submitted confirmation appears.
   - The upload/Submit button is gone.
   - Fixture/file inputs are disabled.
   - “View submission history” is available.
4. Click “View submission history” without refreshing.
   - The newly created batch reference should appear immediately in `/submissions/batches`.
5. As an admin, visit `/reviews/batches`.
   - The batch should appear in “All batches” immediately.
   - It will only appear in “Needs review” once backend validation changes it to `awaiting_review`.

For failure behavior, submit an invalid file or simulate an API failure:
- You should see an error/rejection state.
- The upload button must remain enabled for retry.
- No submitted confirmation should appear.

You can also run the automated browser check:

```powershell
$env:PLAYWRIGHT_PORT='4175'
npm.cmd run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/submissions.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1
```

Yes—there is a disposable local PostgreSQL test DB, but the browser E2E tests do not use it; they mock the API. For a quick manual UI check, use the running dev backend/database your team already uses.

Upload here:

1. Sign in as a submitter/admin.
2. Go to `/submissions/new`.
3. Keep “Single fixture” selected.
4. Select the fixture shown in the dropdown.
5. Under “Fixture package”, upload a `.json` file.

The easiest starting file is already in the app: click **Download JSON template** on that page. Then replace its placeholder values with the exact selected fixture’s date and team names.

Use this minimal package, changing the marked values to match the fixture dropdown exactly:

```json
{
  "contractVersion": "1.0",
  "packageId": "manual-test:submission-state-001",
  "competition": {
    "context": {
      "name": "EXACT COMPETITION NAME",
      "country": "South Africa"
    }
  },
  "season": {
    "context": {
      "name": "EXACT SEASON LABEL"
    }
  },
  "fixtures": [
    {
      "context": {
        "date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
        "teams": [
          { "context": { "name": "EXACT HOME TEAM NAME" } },
          { "context": { "name": "EXACT AWAY TEAM NAME" } }
        ]
      },
      "innings": [
        {
          "context": {
            "ordinal": 0,
            "battingTeam": {
              "context": { "name": "EXACT HOME TEAM NAME" }
            }
          },
          "events": [
            {
              "eventId": "manual-test:delivery:001",
              "occurrenceSequence": 1,
              "overNumber": 0,
              "positionInOver": 0,
              "ballLabel": "0.1",
              "striker": {
                "context": {
                  "name": "Test Batter",
                  "team": { "context": { "name": "EXACT HOME TEAM NAME" } }
                }
              },
              "nonStriker": {
                "context": {
                  "name": "Test Non-striker",
                  "team": { "context": { "name": "EXACT HOME TEAM NAME" } }
                }
              },
              "bowler": {
                "context": {
                  "name": "Test Bowler",
                  "team": { "context": { "name": "EXACT AWAY TEAM NAME" } }
                }
              },
              "runs": { "offBat": 0, "extras": 0, "total": 0 },
              "extras": {}
            }
          ]
```

For the #520 UI fix, the player names do not need to resolve perfectly: after the upload receives a durable receipt, you can verify the submit button disappears and the batch appears in **View submission history** without refreshing. The report may later show validation errors for unknown player names—that is expected for test names.

The isolated test database is:

```text
postgresql://test_user:test_password@127.0.0.1:55432/sport_analytics_test
```

Create/reset/seed it with:

```powershell
npm.cmd run test:database:local
```

That DB is intentionally disposable and is seeded for automated database testing. It is not automatically connected to the frontend; manual browser testing also needs a backend configured to use it and a suitable authenticated submitter/admin account. Avoid using the shared development database for throwaway uploads unless your team agrees.

> which fixture do i submit to?

Use whichever fixture appears in the **Fixture** dropdown on `/submissions/new` for your signed-in submitter account.

Copy its details exactly into the JSON:

- date
- home team
- away team
- competition
- season

For example, if the dropdown says:

```text
2026-08-20 — Wanderers v Strikers — Example Competition, 2026 (T20)
```

use:

```json
"competition": { "context": { "name": "Example Competition", "country": "South Africa" } },
"season": { "context": { "name": "2026" } },
"fixtures": [{
  "context": {
    "date": "2026-08-20",
    "teams": [
      { "context": { "name": "Wanderers" } },
      { "context": { "name": "Strikers" } }
    ]
  }
}]
```

If the dropdown is empty, your account has no authorised fixtures. You’ll need an admin to grant your submitter account a competition scope, or sign in with an admin account.

We have the cause now: the backend is returning HTTP `503`, not rejecting your JSON.

The response is almost certainly:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "BATCH_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "The batch payload could not be stored."
  }
}
```

The local backend’s batch endpoint needs configured object storage for successful uploads. In normal development mode, that storage service is not composed, so `/api/v1/batches` cannot create a durable receipt. The test database alone is not enough—it stores database records, while the uploaded package itself must go to Azure Blob Storage.

So:

- Your JSON is valid.
- The selected fixture data is valid.
- The frontend failure/retry behavior is working.
- A successful manual browser upload cannot be completed against this local backend until the team’s Azure Blob storage configuration/credentials are available.

For #520, the successful path is covered by the focused Playwright E2E test, which mocks the confirmed `202` batch receipt and verifies:

```text
submit batch → success confirmation → Submit removed → history navigation → new batch visible
```

To manually test the success case, use an environment where the backend has working batch object storage configured—typically the deployed/shared environment approved by your team. Do not switch local `NODE_ENV` to production or add Azure credentials without team approval.
